chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: The first night with the Selmer
summary: McRae sweated through a set because he could not hear the new horn, but the sound carried out front.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Called it the "run around," you know. Wind up went out and bought him a snare and went on the bass drum. (humming notes) (Inaudible). So when Selmer came out with this big ad with Coleman Hawkins, every tenor player -- A lot of guys (Inaudible), they couldn't play that. But once I picked it up, I never put it down, because I got rid of -- I left my Conn in the store. Walked out with a Link mouthpiece and the Selmer, and went to work that night. And I kept telling Chick, "I got a new horn." "Yeah, you got one of them Selmers." "Yeah, I (Inaudible) got a Selmer." But I couldn't hear it. It floored me for about two or three hours. I was breaking out in a sweat and I say (inaudible). I think Hilton was playing. He say, "Hey, it sounds good, man. Sounds good." They could hear it, but to me, the sound hadn't came to me like the Conn. I was thinking
